home.title: LIMIT: Representation Learning with Very Limited Resources
home.tagline: When Data, Modalities, Labels, and Computing Resources are Scarce
home.subtitle: ECCV 2026 Workshop

overview.mission: This workshop aims to bring together researchers and practitioners to discuss the latest advances and challenges in representation learning under limited-resource settings. We focus on innovative approaches for learning with scarce data, labels, modalities, and computing resources, including self-supervised, semi-supervised, few-shot, and synthetic data-driven methods.
keyTopics: Recognition, generation, reconstruction, any visual/multi-modal tasks in limited situations
{Self, Semi, Weakly, Un}-supervised learning with very limited resources
{Zero, One, Few}-shot learning with very limited resources
Training convnets, transformers, diffusion, foundation models with relatively fewer resources
Synthetic training with procedural, artificially generated images

callForPapers.title: Call for Papers
callForPapers.subtitle: Submit your research to the LIMIT Workshop

core: Building vision/spatial multi-modal models under limited-resources settings
Synthetic training strategies for vision/spatial multi-modal models
Issues (social bias, privacy and transparency) with real data and labels
Vision+X and multi-modality to accelerate a learning efficiency

submissionGuidelines: Submissions must be handled electronically via the OpenReview submission website
Papers should be longer than 4 pages and up to 14 pages, excluding references, for publication in the Springer proceedings
paperFormat.reviewProcess: All submissions will undergo a double-blind peer review process. Each paper will be reviewed by at least two reviewers from our program committee.
paperFormat.publication: Accepted papers will be published in the Springer proceedings and presented at the workshop.

submission.description: The OpenReview submission website is now open. Please submit your papers through the link below.

callForPapers.bestPaperAwards: We will present Best Paper and Best Student Paper awards to recognize outstanding contributions. Award winners will receive certificates and will be highlighted during the workshop.

faq.question: Can I submit a paper that is under review elsewhere?
faq.answer: No, submissions must be original and not under review at any other conference, workshop, or journal during the review period.

faq.question: What is the page limit for submissions?
faq.answer: Papers should be longer than 4 pages and up to 14 pages, excluding references, for publication in the Springer proceedings.

faq.question: Is the review process double-blind?
faq.answer: Yes, all submissions must be anonymized for double-blind review.

faq.question: Do I need to attend the workshop if my paper is accepted?
faq.answer: Yes, at least one author of each accepted paper must register for and attend the workshop to present the work.
